text:
maria: pushed a WIP terraform module called gpu-fleet-provisioner. it wires mixed-az spot+reserved node groups, per-pool launch templates, and emits a values.yaml for cluster-autoscaler helm. want review on sane defaults for scale policy + drain behavior

jon: link?

maria: https://git.internal/redwood/infra-modules/trees/feat/gpu-fleet-provisioner — main bits are: create a small warm pool, spot pool with buffer, reserved pool for latency-sensitive jobs, and a service account + taint/label conventions. also generates helm values for CA.

sam: quick question — what did you set for scale-down timing? we saw flappy pods last time when scale-down was 5m

maria: default CA args in the module:```
extraArgs:
  --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
  --scale-down-unready-time=15m
  --scale-down-delay-after-add=10m
  --balance-similar-node-groups=true
  --ignore-daemonsets-utilization=false
```
I picked 10m to be conservative but still not hold unused GPUs forever. open to bumping to 12-15m.

lee: +1 on being conservative. also we should ensure we dont evict pods with local checkpoints. add `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false`? last time CA skipped and we had stuck training jobs.

sam: we also need a warm pool param. what about `warm_reserved = 8` for prod and autoscaler should prefer warm pool first via node group priorities?

maria: module supports `warm_size` and emits node group annotation `node.kubernetes.io/group-priority` so CA picks reserved first if available. terraform snippet in the module:```
module "gpu_fleet" {
  source = "git::ssh://git.internal/redwood/infra-modules//gpu_fleet?ref=feat/provisioner"
  region = "eu-west-2"
  warm_size = 8
  min_size = 2
  max_size = 150
  spot_fallback = true
  taint = "redwood/gpu:NoSchedule"
}
```

jon: infra-bot — any CI output from the TF plan + helm lint we ran?

infra-bot: CI: terraform fmt OK, terraform validate OK, helm lint passed (cluster-autoscaler v9.15.0 values). terraform plan: will add 16 resources, modify 1 aws_launch_template, expected new capacity +10 nodes in eu-west-2 staging.

lee: question on spot fallback: if spot capacity is exhausted we fall back to reserved pool, right? what's the burst strategy?

maria: yes — fallback creates nodes in the reserved pool via mixed-instance policy. burst strategy: allocate up to `burst_capacity` (default 20) beyond warm pool before scaling reserved baseline. config keys: `burst_capacity`, `fallback_threshold` (percent of AZs failing to allocate).

sam: can we add a short prewarm window so ephemeral batch jobs don't suffer cold-start? maybe a prewarm hook that keeps N nodes idle for X minutes after scale-down for predicted workload spikes.

maria: added `prewarm_grace` (minutes) to module, default 30. it keeps a small number of replaced nodes in ASG for the grace window by setting lifecycle hooks + termination delay.

jon: cost ask — estimate for warm_size=8 in eu-west-2 using g5.xlarge equivalents? rough calc for monthly: 8 * $1.80 * 24 * 30 = $1036.8 — add spot savings for burst usage.

lee: add a label `redwood/critical=true` for reserved nodes so we can filter in console and alerts. also upstream CA needs `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false` as noted.

maria: updated helm values in the repo. current values snippet:```
controller:
  extraArgs:
    --scale-down-unneeded-time=12m
    --scale-down-unready-time=15m
    --skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false
    --balance-similar-node-groups=true
  resources:
    limits:
      cpu: 200m
      memory: 256Mi
```

sam: can we gate `scale-down-unneeded-time` behind a tf var so dev clusters can be aggressive?

maria: yes it is a module input `ca_scale_down_unneeded_time`. default 12m for prod, 6m for dev.

infra-bot: staging plan dry-run: will provision warm pool (8), spot pool (auto) + reserved fallback. expected nodes: staging 8 -> 18 on test workload. helm chart deploy staging: deployment/cluster-autoscaler will be updated.

jon: any known network or ENI limits with mixed-instance policy across AZs? last month we hit ENI quota in us-west-2 when we spun up all at once.

maria: noted — module includes a `burst_rate_limit` parameter and an orchestration step in `apply` docs recommending staggered subnets per AZ. also we added a pre-check script that queries account ENI quotas and fails plan if projected > 90%. script:```
./tools/check-eni-quota --region eu-west-2 --expected-instances 120
```

lee: propose we add a simple autoscaler health dashboard alert: % Pending pods with gpu request > 0 OR pending > 5 for > 2m -> pager. helps catch capacity holes.

sam: agree. add also preemption metric alert for spot eviction spikes.

maria: action items: 1) merge module to staging branch, 2) deploy CA helm values to staging with `--scale-down-unneeded-time=12m`, 3) run canary in eu-west-2 with warm_size=8 and burst_capacity=20 for 24h, 4) verify ENI quotas and preemption metrics, 5) if green, promote to prod and open reserved commit ticket for long-running training workloads.

jon: +1. canary window 24h starts on merge? schedule at 0200 UTC to avoid disruptions.

maria: will open PR and tag @sam @lee for rollout. thanks all :rocket:
